api.unreachable: The API could not be reached.

intro.title: Three libraries, zero references between them
intro.description: This application installs DotNetBoost.Settings, DotNetBoost.Media and DotNetBoost.MultiLingual from NuGet. None depends on another, there is no shared kernel package, and no integration package pairs any two of them. Everything here is produced by application code composing them.

composition.title: Where the composition happens
composition.dbContext: One PostgreSQL database, one DbContext, and three independent {apply} calls. Remove a library and you delete its one line; nothing else in the file changes.
composition.mediaText: Per-language alt text for an uploaded file. Both libraries address a subject by {pair}, so a media file's own GUID becomes the subject of translation rows. {withAltText} of {imageCount} attached images have alt text. No new table, no integration package.
composition.branding: The group's name in every language, and its logo. Neither is a settings value: the name's other languages are translation rows, and the logo is a media attachment on an owner with no table behind it. A projector joins all three onto the group's own endpoint.

languageAlert.title: Switch the language in any page header
languageAlert.description: Every product name, description and image alt text is re-read in that language — Arabic flips the whole shell to RTL. The API resolves it from Accept-Language. The dashboard's own labels follow the same selector.

categories.title: Categories
categories.description: The application's own entity. Name and description are not columns on this table — they are translation rows, returned already filled in for the language in the header.

products.title: Products
products.description: Name and description are translation rows; images are attachments in the media library. Neither library knows the other exists.

confirmDelete.title: Delete {name}?
confirmDelete.description: This cannot be undone. A product's images and their alt text go with it — written out by hand, because nothing cascades across library boundaries.

categoryEditor.description: Slug is a column. Text is translation rows. The banner is a media attachment.

slug.label: Slug
slug.help: Not translated — a URL segment should be the same string in every language, which is what [NotMultiLingual] declares.

saveFirst.title: Save first to attach media
saveFirst.description: An attachment needs the category's key, which it does not have until it is saved.

productEditor.description: SKU and price are columns. Name and description are translation rows. Images are media attachments.

saveFirst.title: Save first to attach media
saveFirst.description: An attachment needs the product's key, which it does not have until it is saved.

translationFields.name: Name
translationFields.note: Stored as translation rows, not as columns on this entity. Clearing a field removes the row rather than storing an empty string.

languages.title: Languages

card.description: Served by MapLanguageEndpoints() from DotNetBoost.MultiLingual.API — library endpoints, not ones this application wrote. Direction is stored alongside the language, which is what lets the shell flip to RTL without a hardcoded list of codes in the client.

languages.empty: No languages yet. Add one to start writing content.

badge.baseTooltip: The base language: its values live in the entities' own columns rather than in the translations table.

confirmPurge.title: Delete everything written in {name}?
confirmPurge.description: Every translation in {code} is removed, across every entity. The language itself stays, and content falls back to the default until it is filled in again.
confirmPurge.baseNote: This is the base language, so its values live in the entities' own columns and are not touched.

confirmDelete.title: Delete {name}?
confirmDelete.description: The language and everything written in it go. The API refuses if it is the default.

toast.addedDefault: {code} is now the default — content falls back to it.
toast.addedOther: Content can now be written in {code}.
toast.savedInactive: It is inactive, so content is no longer served in it.
toast.promotedDescription: Missing translations fall back to it, and the language that held the role was demoted.
toast.purgedDescription: {code} still exists; everything written in it is gone.

form.descriptionAdd: A new language starts with no translations. Existing content falls back to the default until each row is filled in.
form.descriptionEdit: The code is the language's identity and cannot change; everything written in it is keyed by it.

code.label: Code
code.description: ISO 639-1, optionally with a region: en, ar, pt-BR.

name.label: Name
name.description: Shown in the language picker, written in the language itself.

direction.label: Direction
direction.descriptionNew: Left as “from the code”, the API takes it from the runtime's culture data — ar, he, fa and ur come back right to left.
direction.descriptionEdit: Changing this flips the shell for everyone reading in this language.

active.label: Active
active.description: When off, content is no longer served in it. The default language cannot be deactivated.

makeDefault.label: Make it the default
makeDefault.descriptionFirst: The first language created is always the default — there is nothing to fall back to otherwise.
makeDefault.descriptionOther: Demotes whichever language holds the role now.

page.title: Every uploaded file
page.description: One row per upload, whatever it is attached to. Search by name, narrow by category or tag, sort, and page — all of it in the query the API is asked, not in the rows already on screen. This is DotNetBoost.Media's own browser, unchanged; the only addition is alt text, which comes from DotNetBoost.MultiLingual and is edited from a file's details.

browser.loadError: Could not load the media library

emptyFiltered.title: Nothing matches this filter
emptyFiltered.description: Try a different search, category or tag.

confirmDelete.title: Delete {fileName}?
confirmDelete.description: The bytes are removed from the storage backend, and every link to the file goes with them. {usage} With soft delete on — the default — the row is kept as a record that the file existed, but the content is gone either way.
confirmDelete.usedByOne: It is attached to {entity}, which loses it.
confirmDelete.usedByMany: It is attached to {count} entities, and all of them lose it: {entities}.

detail.description: Everything the media row records. The bytes, their size and where they live are fixed — replacing content means a new upload.
detail.directLinkTitle: A signed, expiring link straight to the storage backend

fileName.label: File name
fileName.description: The name the file is offered under. The stored path does not change.

category.label: Category
category.description: A coarse bucket. Changing it does not move the stored bytes.

tags.label: Tags
tags.description: Up to 32, each 64 characters, no commas.

usedBy.label: Used by
usedBy.descriptionOne: Which entities this file is attached to, and what each uses it for. Click a role to remove that link — the file itself stays.
usedBy.descriptionMany: One file, several entities — nothing is copied, they all point at the same bytes. Click a role to remove that one link; deleting the file removes it from all of them.
usedBy.none: Nothing — it is in the library, waiting to be attached.

storage.title: Where the bytes are
storage.description: Not shown by the API's own responses, on purpose — the storage layout is not a client's business. This dashboard talks to the API as an administrator would.

upload.title: Upload a file
upload.descriptionOwner: Stored and attached to {entity} in one step.
upload.descriptionPlain: Stored through POST api/media. The name, size and type are recorded from the file itself.
upload.dropzone: Drop a file here, or click to choose

category.label: Category
category.description: A coarse bucket — avatars, invoices, product-images. It also leads the storage path.

tags.label: Tags
tags.description: Up to 32, each 64 characters, no commas.

checks.title: What the API checks
checks.description: The size is measured as the bytes arrive, the type is verified against the file's own leading bytes, and executables are refused. A file that fails any of those comes back as a problem detail rather than being stored.

picker.title: Media for {entity}
picker.descriptionFixedRole: Pick the file this {entity} should use as its {role}, or upload one — it is stored and attached in one step. {shared}
picker.descriptionPlain: Attach a file that is already in the library, or upload a new one — it is stored and attached in one step. {shared}
picker.shared: A file may belong to several entities at once; attaching it here does not take it off anything else.

hint.undeclared: This entity declares no roles, so any name will do.
hint.multiple: Appended to the end, in order.
hint.single: Becomes the one file in this role, replacing whatever held it.

altText.title: Alt text and caption
altText.subtitle: Stored by DotNetBoost.MultiLingual, not by the media library.
altText.missing: {n} language without alt text | {n} languages without alt text

altText.label: Alt text
altText.description: Required for accessibility, and different in every language.

altText.caption: Caption
altText.note: Clearing a field removes the stored row rather than storing an empty string.

toast.readFailed: Could not read the alt text
toast.saveFailed: Could not save the alt text

attachments.missingAltText: Some of these have no alt text in this language — add it from the Media page.
attachments.noRoles: This entity declares no media roles.

settings.unknownGroup: No settings group is mounted at "{route}".

branding.label: Branding
branding.description: How the store presents itself. Saved changes take effect on the next read — no restart, no redeploy.

storeName.label: Store name
storeName.description: Shown in the sidebar header, in place of the sample's own name.

headerLogoSize.label: Header logo size
headerLogoSize.description: How large the logo is drawn in the sidebar header, in pixels. Must be between 16 and 64 — the API refuses anything outside, and this control reads that range from the group's schema.

catalog.label: Catalog
catalog.description: How the catalogue is presented. These are read on every listing, so a change is visible immediately.

conflict.title: These settings changed while you were editing

toast.savedDescription: The new values are live — no redeploy needed.
toast.conflictProblem: Someone else changed these settings while you were editing. Nothing was saved, and your edits are still here.
toast.conflictDescription: Reload the latest values, or re-apply your edits on top of them.

media.title: Media
media.description: Not a setting. The logo is a media attachment on an owner that has no table anywhere — which a foreign key could not express, and which the media library is perfectly happy with, because an owner is only ever two strings it never tries to resolve.
media.outsideSave: Outside this form's Save, and outside the group's ETag and audit trail — the three things storing a file id in a setting would have bought. Given up for a single source of truth: detaching the logo and the store having no logo are the same statement.

groupText.title: Store name in other languages
groupText.descriptionWithDefault: The default language ({code}) is the value in the form above — it lives in the settings row. These are translation rows, and a language with nothing stored falls back to it.
groupText.descriptionPlain: These are translation rows. A language with nothing stored falls back to the default.
groupText.missing: {n} language not translated | {n} languages not translated
groupText.onlyOneLanguage: There is only one language, so there is nothing to translate yet. Add another on the Languages page.
groupText.note: Stored as {subject} rows, one per language — the same subject the logo is attached to.

toast.savedDescription: Reading in those languages now returns them.
